scenario_text: A government-owned insurance company needs a claims processing portal for rural customers. All requirements have already been documented in a 200-page RFP. The portal must comply with IRDAI regulations. The team has 15 developers, funding is approved for 18 months, and the requirements will not change once signed off.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a user-friendly claims processing portal for rural customers
requirements.business_justification: Rural customers have limited access to digital services; a user-friendly portal increases adoption and reduces support requests
requirements.assumptions: Users have basic computer literacy and access to internet-enabled devices
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal has a simple and intuitive interface, with clear instructions and minimal navigation steps

requirements.statement: The system shall ensure compliance with IRDAI regulations for claims processing
requirements.business_justification: Non-compliance can result in fines and reputational damage; regulatory compliance is essential for business continuity
requirements.assumptions: IRDAI regulations are up-to-date and publicly available
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal meets all IRDAI requirements for claims processing, as verified through regular audits and compliance checks

requirements.statement: The system shall provide secure data storage and transmission for claims processing
requirements.business_justification: Data breaches can result in financial losses and reputational damage; secure data storage and transmission are essential for customer trust
requirements.assumptions: Data encryption and secure transmission protocols are implemented correctly
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal stores and transmits claims data securely, as verified through regular penetration testing and vulnerability assessments
applicable_regulations: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §4(e) (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]
IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, 2023 §3.5 (IRDAI/GA&HR/GDL/MISC/88/04/2023) [issued 24 Apr 2023]

requirements.statement: The system shall be scalable to handle increased traffic and claims volume
requirements.business_justification: Increased traffic and claims volume can result in system downtime and decreased customer satisfaction; scalability ensures business continuity
requirements.assumptions: Traffic and claims volume will increase gradually over time
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal can handle increased traffic and claims volume without significant performance degradation, as measured through regular load testing and benchmarking

requirements.statement: The system shall allow rural customers to track the status of their claims in real-time.
requirements.business_justification: The portal is for rural customers, implying they may not have access to regular internet or may be less tech-savvy, so they need to be able to track their claims easily.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall display the current status of a claim on the customer's dashboard within 2 seconds of login.

requirements.statement: The system shall notify customers and insurance company staff via email/SMS when a claim is submitted, processed, or rejected.
requirements.business_justification: The portal is for claims processing, which involves multiple stakeholders and steps, so notifications are necessary to keep everyone informed.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall send a notification to the customer's registered email address within 1 minute of claim submission.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow insurance company staff to cancel or correct claims within a 30-day window.
requirements.business_justification: Claims processing involves human error, so staff need to be able to correct or cancel claims if necessary.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall allow staff to cancel or correct a claim within 30 days of submission, with a clear audit trail.

requirements.statement: The system shall handle failed checks or unavailable external services by retrying the operation after 30 minutes.
requirements.business_justification: Claims processing involves external services and checks, which may fail or be unavailable, so the system needs to handle these exceptions.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall retry a failed check or external service call after 30 minutes, with a maximum of 3 retries.

requirements.statement: The system shall be configured to store claims data for a minimum of 5 years, as per IRDAI regulations.
requirements.business_justification: The portal must comply with IRDAI regulations, which include data retention requirements.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall store claims data for a minimum of 5 years, with a clear audit trail of data access and modification.

requirements.statement: The system shall be designed to handle a minimum of 10,000 concurrent users, with a maximum response time of 2 seconds.
requirements.business_justification: The portal is for rural customers, implying a large user base, and the system needs to perform well under load.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall handle a minimum of 10,000 concurrent users, with a maximum response time of 2 seconds, as measured by a load testing tool.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a clear and concise user interface for customers with visual impairments, as per WCAG 2.1 guidelines.
requirements.business_justification: The portal is for rural customers, who may include people with disabilities, so the system needs to be accessible.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall meet all WCAG 2.1 guidelines for accessibility, with a clear and concise user interface for customers with visual impairments.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide real-time monitoring and logging of claims processing, with alerts for staff when issues arise.
requirements.business_justification: Claims processing involves multiple stakeholders and steps, so real-time monitoring and logging are necessary to identify issues quickly.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system shall provide real-time monitoring and logging of claims processing, with alerts for staff when issues arise, as measured by a monitoring tool.

justifications.gives_up: Waterfall assumes the system stands on its own, and that the users do not want to be involved throughout — neither is true here, so that part of its design earns nothing on this project.

sdlc.summary: The project's characteristics, such as a fixed delivery window, stable requirements, and user involvement, align with the Waterfall approach. The system's infrastructure component nature and scalability requirements also support this choice. The project's need for user representatives and system integration, however, do not fit the Waterfall model as well. Overall, the Waterfall approach is the best fit for this project, with a FITS score of 83% (10/12).

source.title: Cyber Security Framework in Banks

risk_register.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for the system
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices §28 (RBI/2023-24/107) [issued 07 Nov 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall have a disaster recovery arrangement with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, tested periodically under the bank's business continuity plan.

risk_register.title: Cyber incidents reported to CERT-In within 6 hours
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall support reporting cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of their being noticed, with a copy to the sector regulator.

risk_register.title: ICT system logs kept for a rolling 180 days within India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(iv) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep logs of all its ICT components securely for a rolling 180 days, within India, and make them available to CERT-In on request.

risk_register.title: Insurer's ICT logs, critical and business data stored in India
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, 2023 §14 (IRDAI/GA&HR/GDL/MISC/88/04/2023) [issued 24 Apr 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall keep its ICT infrastructure logs and all critical and business data in India, with logs retained for a rolling 180 days.

risk_register.title: A grievance redressal mechanism for customers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Direction on Outsourcing of Information Technology Services §7 (RBI/2023-24/102) [issued 10 Apr 2023])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall let customers raise complaints and disputes, track them to resolution, and show the contact details of the designated grievance redressal officer.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.title: Unverified regulation on REQ-001
risk_register.cause: REQ-001 names IRDAI, which nothing in the knowledge base supports.
risk_register.consequence: The design rests on a regulation nobody has checked applies, or exists in that form.
risk_register.mitigation: Have compliance confirm the named regulation and its applicable clause.

risk_register.title: Unverified regulation on REQ-002
risk_register.cause: REQ-002 names IRDAI, which nothing in the knowledge base supports.
risk_register.consequence: The design rests on a regulation nobody has checked applies, or exists in that form.
risk_register.mitigation: Have compliance confirm the named regulation and its applicable clause.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.title: Role-based access with least privilege for staff and administrators
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.3 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall grant staff access by role on a least-privilege, need-to-know basis, and enforce maker-checker approval for sensitive operations.

risk_register.title: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall encrypt customer and transaction data at rest and in transit using algorithms and key lengths approved under the bank's cryptographic policy.

risk_register.title: Strong customer authentication — a second factor at login and for high-value actions
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §34 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall authenticate customers with at least two factors at login, and require step-up authentication for transactions above the organisation-approved risk threshold.

risk_register.title: Regulatory Compliance Risk
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "IRDAI regulations"
risk_register.consequence: Non-compliance with regulations could lead to fines, penalties, or even project cancellation
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.

risk_register.title: Resource Management Risk
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "funding is approved for 18 months"
risk_register.consequence: Insufficient funding or resource constraints could lead to project delays or cancellation
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.

risk_register.title: Scope Creep Risk
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "requirements will not change once signed off"
risk_register.consequence: If requirements do change, it could lead to scope creep, delays, and cost overruns
risk_register.mitigation: Review with the project manager.
evidence: requirements will not change once signed off

risk_register.title: Contact details handled without stated protection
risk_register.cause: Contact details appears in REQ-006 and no requirement encrypts, masks or restricts it.
risk_register.consequence: Exposure of Contact details — a reportable personal data breach.
risk_register.mitigation: Add a requirement protecting Contact details (encryption, masking, access control).

risk_register.title: Input validated and secure coding practices applied
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: OWASP ASVS (industry practice; not in the knowledge base)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall validate all input on the server side and be built and tested against the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard.

risk_register.title: Only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose is collected
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 §6 (Act No. 22 of 2023) [as enacted]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall collect only the personal data necessary for each specified purpose and reject or discard fields not required for it.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall forward security events to the bank's security operations monitoring and raise alerts on anomalous access or activity.

risk_register.title: Sessions time out and repeated failed logins lock the account
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §53 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall end inactive sessions after a defined timeout and temporarily lock access after repeated failed login attempts.
